Live preview

Register a view with location: 'preview' to make the Split preview button available. It opens a second surface next to the active editor; narrow screens stack the two surfaces. Extensions own the document model, preview renderer, and synchronization. context.views.open('preview-id') opens a registered preview programmatically. If several preview views are registered, users can select them in the preview pane. The editor and preview scroll independently, while editor tabs remain visible.

Optional size and scale controls

Set viewport on a preview view to let Edy wrap its rendered node in a configurable logical viewport. Width and height are CSS pixels; visual zoom does not change them. Automatic scaling fits both dimensions into the available space without enlarging above 100%. Manual scaling uses a percentage and provides scrollbars when the scaled viewport exceeds the space available. Size choices are supplied and named by the extension, not by Edy:

context.views.register('preview', {
  title: 'Preview',
  location: 'preview',
  viewport: {
    width: 1024, height: 768, scale: 'auto',
    minWidth: 200, maxWidth: 4096,
    minHeight: 100, maxHeight: 4096,
    minScale: 25, maxScale: 200,
    presets: [
      { id: 'phone', label: 'Phone', width: 375, height: 667 },
      { id: 'desktop', label: 'Desktop', width: 1024, height: 768 },
    ],
    onChange: ({ width, height, scale }) => {
      console.log(width, height, scale);
    },
  },
  render: () => createPreviewFrame({
    src: '/my-preview.html',
    title: 'Preview',
    allowedOrigin: 'null',
    operations: [],
  }),
});

width, height, and limits are positive integers. Defaults are 1024 × 768, width limits 200–4096, height limits 100–4096 and manual scale limits 25–200%. scale is 'auto' or an integer percentage within its limits. Preset IDs must be unique and dimensions must satisfy the limits. Invalid configuration is rejected at registration; UI values outside the limits are rejected. onChange runs after user changes and receives the logical dimensions and 'auto' or the manual percentage; automatic adjustments due to container resizing do not fire it. State is independent per view and instance and is retained when the preview is closed and reopened while registered.

Return the preview node directly, or { element, dispose } as shown below, and size its content to fill the viewport. For an iframe, its content viewport matches the logical dimensions and responsive CSS can react to changes. This does not emulate device pixel ratio, touch input, browser engines or other device characteristics. Without viewport, existing views retain their original rendering.

For a sandboxed HTML preview, import createPreviewFrame from src/index.js. Use an explicit operation allowlist and validate messages. The included demoExtension listens for preview readiness and forwards edited text using postMessage. The frame renders text with textContent, never as HTML.

const preview = createPreviewFrame({
  src: '/my-preview.html',
  title: 'Preview',
  allowedOrigin: 'null',
  operations: ['ready', 'update'],
  validateMessage: (message) => message.operation === 'ready',
});
const subscription = preview.onMessage(() => {
  preview.postMessage({ operation: 'update', payload: { text: 'Hello' } });
});
// Return this from a view renderer:
return {
  element: preview.element,
  dispose() {
    subscription.dispose();
    preview.dispose();
  },
};

The default sandbox has an opaque origin (null); Edy checks the exact frame window and allowed message operations. If using allow-same-origin, the preview must be served from a different origin and allowedOrigin must match its URL. Never send credentials or unrestricted host services into a preview. Preview code must validate messages from its parent as well. Limit payload sizes and treat all preview content as untrusted.
